meta.name: splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure
meta.displayName: Splunk TA for SAP LogServ on Azure

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Azure Storage Queue inputs that ingest SAP LogServ blobs from Azure via Event Grid blob-created notifications — the Azure counterpart to the AWS SQS-based S3 input. Install on Heavy Forwarders.

entity.label: Input name
entity.help: A unique identifier for this input. Letters, digits, dashes, and underscores only.

validators.errorMsg: Input name must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, dashes, or underscores.

entity.label: Interval (seconds)
entity.help: How often the input polls the queue (10–3600 seconds). Each firing drains the queue up to the time budget and the Max blobs per fire cap. Default 60 seconds.

validators.errorMsg: Interval must be between 10 and 3600 seconds.

entity.label: Storage account
entity.help: Azure Storage account name hosting the Storage Queue (and the LogServ blobs). 3–24 lowercase letters/digits, e.g. logservprod01. Obtain from your SAP support contact. Used to build https://<account>.queue.core.windows.net/.

validators.errorMsg: Storage account name must be 3–24 lowercase letters or digits.

entity.label: Queue name
entity.help: Name of the Storage Queue that the Event Grid Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated subscription delivers notifications to. Obtain from your SAP support contact. 3–63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; must start and end with a letter or digit.

validators.errorMsg: Queue name must be 3–63 chars: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

entity.label: SAS token
entity.help: Shared Access Signature for the storage account, covering BOTH Queue (process + delete messages) AND Blob (read). Obtain from your SAP support contact. Paste the SAS query string (with or without a leading '?'). Stored encrypted in passwords.conf. On Edit the field shows '******'; saving without changing it preserves the existing token. If your LogServ SAS is queue-only, supply a SAS that also grants Blob-read here — the consumer must fetch blob content.

entity.label: Target index
entity.help: Splunk index the ingested events are written to. Defaults to sap_logserv_logs (the index the LogServ dashboards read).

validators.errorMsg: Index name must start with a lowercase letter or digit and contain only lowercase letters, digits, dashes, or underscores.

entity.label: Sourcetype
entity.help: Fixed at sap_logserv_logs. The add-on HARD-CODES this sourcetype (it is NOT read from the input stanza), since the Data TA's index-time routing / Filters / cloud_provider+splunk_solution stamping all key on it. Shown read-only (disabled when editing an existing input); leave it as sap_logserv_logs.

validators.errorMsg: Sourcetype must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, colons, dots, dashes, or underscores.

entity.label: Messages per dequeue
entity.help: How many queue messages to retrieve per dequeue call (Azure caps this at 32). Default 32.

validators.errorMsg: Messages per dequeue must be between 1 and 32.

entity.label: Visibility timeout (seconds)
entity.help: How long a dequeued message stays invisible to other consumers while this input processes it. Set comfortably above the worst-case single-blob processing time. Range 30–604800 (7 days). Default 300.

validators.errorMsg: Visibility timeout must be between 30 and 604800 seconds.

entity.label: Max blobs per fire
entity.help: Safety cap on blobs ingested per firing, bounding burst load during backlog drain. The input also stops at a per-firing time budget. Range 1–100000. Default 500.

validators.errorMsg: Max blobs per fire must be between 1 and 100000.

entity.label: Poison threshold
entity.help: A message redelivered more than this many times (Azure's DequeueCount) is treated as poison — moved to the dead-letter queue if one is configured, otherwise dropped — so a permanently-bad blob can't loop forever. Range 1–100. Default 5.

validators.errorMsg: Poison threshold must be between 1 and 100.

entity.label: Include filters
entity.help: Optional comma-separated substrings applied to the blob path (Event Grid subject) as a cheap pre-filter — only blobs whose subject contains at least one substring are downloaded. Leave empty to accept all LogServ blobs. The canonical clz_dir/clz_subdir allow/deny policy lives in the Data TA Filters tab; this only avoids downloading obviously-irrelevant blobs.

validators.errorMsg: Include filters must be less than 4096 characters.

entity.label: Exclude filters
entity.help: Optional comma-separated substrings applied to the blob path (Event Grid subject); a blob whose subject matches any of these is skipped (not downloaded). Exclude always wins over include.

validators.errorMsg: Exclude filters must be less than 4096 characters.

entity.label: Dead-letter queue
entity.help: Optional Storage Queue name (in the same account) to move poison messages to instead of dropping them. Leave empty to drop poison messages after logging. Storage Queues have no native dead-letter facility, so this is a manual sink for inspection.

validators.errorMsg: Dead-letter queue must be empty or a valid queue name (3–63 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).

entity.label: Verify SSL
entity.help: Verify the TLS certificate of the Azure Storage endpoints. Leave enabled for production (Azure uses valid public certificates).
